singleSourced.context: You can swap between the original low-poly "SD" character models and more detailed "HD" ones, but even the HD models have been painstakingly retrofitted with the classic game's animation routines, so they don't look out of place.

"Which," he continues, "Is why I am also so proud to announce that Hardcore will be coming to WoW Forever as well."

While this isn't all too surprising on the face of it—Classic Hardcore proved to be incredibly popular—it will be interesting.

singleSourced.context: It's an experience designed to feel more relaxed and easy-going, where the level cap remains at 60 indefinitely, and catching up is just a case of playing the game as normal: "We don't want to race ahead and leave our accomplishments, our gear, and our friends behind," Longdale explains.

singleSourced.context: Longdale is playing the nostalgia card: "We are all going to meet up on our original continents and embark on the journey to 60 - and stay at 60." Despite this, Blizzard has already laid out its plans for a first year of updates.

singleSourced.context: Over on r/WoW, the top comments refer to "Blizzard dodging giving people High Elves like a pro," or simply note, "Skyborne about to upset everyone." There's plenty of excitement for the possibility to finally create an Undead Paladin, however.
While it's not the only indicator of success, the $150 World of Warcraft Forever Collector's Edition is already sold out on the Blizzard store.
